module: Starter template for writing a vehicle controller. A controller is a Lua module placed in lua/vehicle/controller/, declared in the jbeam (`controller` section with `fileName`, and optionally `name`) and loaded by `controller.lua`. Lifecycle: `init(jbeamData)` on creation (jbeamData = the declaration merged with the jbeam data bearing the controller's name), then `initSecondStage`, `initSounds`, `initLastStage` (optional) once the other systems are ready; on reset, `reset(jbeamData)` (or, if absent, `init` is called again) as well as `resetLastStage` and `resetSounds`. In operation: `update(dt)` every physics step, `updateWheelsIntermediate(dt)`, `updateFixedStep(dt)` at a fixed 100 Hz step, `updateGFX(dt)` every graphics frame. Only the functions actually exported in M are called. Other optional hooks: debugDraw, beamBroken, beamDeformed, nodeCollision, onCouplerFound/Attached/Detached, onGameplayEvent, settingsChanged, serialize/deserialize.
usage:
local M = {}
M.type = "auxiliary"
local function init(jbeamData)
  -- read jbeamData.myKey
end
local function updateGFX(dt)
end
M.init = init
M.reset = init
M.updateGFX = updateGFX
return M
notes: `M.type`: "auxiliary" for an ordinary controller; "main" designates the main controller (only one per vehicle, never hot-loadable).

controller.lua itself adds `name`, `typeName`, `hasCustomName`, `manualOrder` (jbeam key `manualOrder`) and `order` to the module after init. A controller can define `M.relevantDevice` (name of a powertrain device) or `M.defaultOrder` to influence the call order.
The beam break hook must be called `beamBroken` (and not beamBroke) to be detected.
In the template, onCouplerFound and onCouplerAttached are commented out with fewer arguments than those actually passed by controller.lua (nodeDist for Found; attachSpeed, attachEnergy for Attached).
If a controller dynamically adds or removes `M.update` & co, it must call `controller.cacheAllControllerFunctions()`.
The commented-out functions of the template are not exported; only init, reset and updateGFX are active.

type.desc: "auxiliary" in the template (secondary controller). "main" for the vehicle's main controller.

init.desc: Called by controller.lua when the controller is created (and on reset if `reset` does not exist). Empty body in the template; this is where the jbeam keys are read.

jbeamData.desc: Controller jbeam data (fileName, name, custom keys...).

reset.desc: Called on vehicle reset (resetSecondStage step of controller.lua). Empty body in the template.

jbeamData.desc: Same jbeam data as for init.

updateGFX.desc: Called every graphics frame. Empty body in the template. The variants `update` (physics step), `updateWheelsIntermediate` and `updateFixedStep` (100 Hz) are provided as comments.
